record.context_brief: Classification of MDS and MDR codes
record.original_question: Classify all maximum-distance-separable codes, meaning codes that meet the Singleton bound d ≤ n − k + 1, and all maximum-distance-with-respect-to-rank linear codes over principal ideal rings, meaning codes that meet the analogous bound d(C) ≤ n − k + 1 where k is the rank of the code, across the classes of alphabets considered in the paper.

evidence.quote: Theorem 6.1. Let C be a code over an alphabet A with length n, minimum distance d and size k = log|A|(C). Then d ≤ n − k + 1.
Codes meeting this bound are called Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) codes.

Theorem 6.3. Let C be a linear code over a principal ideal ring, then d(C) ≤ n − k + 1 where k is the rank of the code. Codes meeting this bound are called Maximum Distance with respect to Rank (MDR).
Open Question 6.4. Find and classify all MDS and MDR codes over various classes of alphabets.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be an alphabet, which is either a finite set of size |A| ≥ 2 or a finite (commutative) principal ideal ring R. A code of length n over A is a subset C ⊆ A^n; when A = R is a ring, a linear code C is an R-submodule of R^n, and its rank is the smallest cardinality of a generating set of C as an R-module. The Hamming distance between x, y ∈ A^n is d(x, y) = |{i : x_i ≠ y_i}|, and the minimum distance of C is d(C) = min{d(x, y) : x, y ∈ C, x ≠ y}.

Set k = log_{|A|}|C| when A is a finite alphabet, and let k be the rank of C when C is a linear code over a finite principal ideal ring. Then in both settings one has the Singleton-type bound d(C) ≤ n − k + 1. Codes attaining this bound are called Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) in the alphabet case, and Maximum Distance with respect to Rank (MDR) in the linear-over-PIR case.

Problem. Classify (give existence parameters and, up to suitable equivalence, an enumeration of) all MDS codes over finite alphabets and all MDR linear codes over finite principal ideal rings. Concretely, determine the complete set of admissible parameters (n, k, d = n − k + 1) and, for each admissible parameter triple, describe all such codes up to monomial/module-equivalence, across the classes of alphabets and principal ideal rings under consideration (in particular finite fields, Galois rings, finite chain rings, and general finite principal ideal rings).
artifact.category_tag: MDS and MDR codes over rings
artifact.status_search_result: A full classification remains open. Even over finite fields, the MDS conjecture (the main classification question for MDS codes) is unresolved in general, despite Ball's proof for prime fields. Over finite chain rings, Galois rings, and principal ideal rings, partial existence results, constructions of infinite families (including self-dual MDS/MDR codes), and necessary/sufficient existence conditions are known, but no complete classification across all these alphabet classes is available.

status_evidence.title: MDS codes over finite principal ideal rings
status_evidence.snippet: Necessary and sufficient conditions on the existence of MDS codes over principal ideal rings are presented, and infinite families are constructed.
status_evidence.claim: Existence results and families are known, but a complete classification is not given.

status_evidence.title: MDS and Self-dual Codes over Rings
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs infinite families of MDS self-dual codes over finite chain rings, formal power series and principal ideal rings.
status_evidence.claim: Research provides constructions rather than a full classification, indicating the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Matrix graphs and MRD codes over finite principal ideal rings
status_evidence.snippet: Studies rank-metric/MRD codes over finite principal ideal rings, an active research direction.
status_evidence.claim: Topic remains an active area of investigation.
